children: Shares of Palantir Technologies (PLTR, Financials), a software business that focuses on data analytics and artificial intelligence, were up $4.76 to about $182.40. That move got notice, but there was another part of the story: Options traders were leaning toward calls.

Volume was roughly 210,000 contracts, about usual for the stock. The interesting thing was the ratio of calls to puts. The put/call ratio declined to 0.37, significantly below the normal level of about 0.72.
Doesn't mean the stock will continue to rise. But it does imply traders were looking for a little greater upside exposure than they normally are.

What makes the scenario a bit more fascinating is that volatility has not gone crazy. Thirty-day implied volatility was around 46.85 percent, a shade higher on the day, and still in the bottom quartile of its range over the previous year. The options market was pricing in a move of about $5.38 a day.
So the message from options traders is pretty simple. There's greater interest on the upside but traders aren't pricing in a big shock just yet.

Now it's the stock's turn to do its thing. If Palantir continues to rise and call demand is high, the options activity could be a fun thing to watch. But that optimistic strategy could flip fast if the surge loses steam.
The options market is leaning one way for now. Whether such assessment is correct will depend on the next move in the stock.

title: Palantir Stock Gets a Bullish Options Signal as Shares Jump 2.7%
